precepts.text: Mattathias had five sons, Joannan and Jonathan among them, John and John; the same name in one family was common in Israel.
precepts.point: Israel named sons the same name: Mattathias had Joannan and Jonathan, there were three Marys at the cross and Simons everywhere, so two Zerubbabels is no puzzle.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Matthew names Christ's family: “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” Mary his mother and Mary his aunt at the cross, a brother named Simon among Simons everywhere: Israel used the same names over and over, even inside one family. The Maccabees prove it.

“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest.” “And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: Simon; called Thassi: Judas, who was called Maccabeus: Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus.” Stop at Jonathan. Joannan and Jonathan are the same name: John and John, two sons of one father. Like George Foreman naming his sons George, George, George and George.

So it was a common thing for Israel to name sons the same name. You had Mary and Mary, John and John, John the Baptist too; they loved that name. You had Simon Iscariot, Simon the Canaanite, Simon Peter, and Christ's own brother Simon. That is why two Zerubbabels in the genealogies is no puzzle at all.

precepts.text: Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. That is what a man in his truth is going to do. He is going to give his life. That is his time. That is his patience. That is his problems. That is his traumas. You sisters as well, you are going to give your lives for that. Everything should revolve around being an Israelite. I had a conversation with a brother and he was asking me how he normalizes the lifestyle of an Israelite. And the question itself was the answer. Normalize that in your everyday life. When you wake up in the morning, you are an Israelite. You are not a black man in America. That is just what you have been labeled as. So the same way that you grew up and were admonished in media with being a negro in America, you have got to reverse that and admonish yourself in what an Israelite is, the Israelite culture. You have got to put yourself in those shoes at every given moment. Your thought process has to be an Israelite man, not a man in America. And call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time. That is how you are going to normalize what it is to be an Israelite, a person that is keeping God's commandments. So shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name. That is how we are going to receive that name. That is how we are going to break those generational curses that we have been stigmatized to.
precepts.point: So now we see, okay, I see the mistake that they made. I am not going to make that same mistake. I am going to be better than the men before me, to the best of my ability, with the spirit that the Lord gave me.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
The Bible has given us all the instructions we need to fix ourselves, and the ultimate fix to all of our problems is remembering and keeping the laws of God. Mattathias told his sons: “Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

That is what a man in his truth is going to do: give his life. That is his time, his patience, his problems, his traumas. Sisters as well, you are going to give your lives for that. Everything should revolve around being an Israelite.

A brother asked how he could normalize the lifestyle of an Israelite, and the question itself was the answer: normalize it in your everyday life. When you wake up in the morning, you are an Israelite. You are not a black man in America; that is just what you have been labeled. The same way you grew up admonished by the media in being a negro in America, you have to reverse that and admonish yourself in what an Israelite is, the Israelite culture. Your thought process has to be an Israelite man, not a man in America.

“Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time”. That is Romans 15:4: the things written aforetime were written for our learning. Remembering the acts of our fathers is how you normalize what it is to be an Israelite, a person keeping God's commandments. We see where they overcame and where they were punished, and we say, I see the mistake they made, I am not going to make it; I am going to be better than the men before me.

“so shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name”. That is how we receive that name, and how we break the generational curses we have been stigmatized with.

precepts.text: Now hath pride and rebuke gotten strength; my sons, be ye zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.
precepts.point: Mattathias had five sons, and the class is on the day of Simon, so Simon is not forgotten: Judas was the hammer and Simon was the hand behind it.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Mattathias had five sons: Joannan, Simon, Judas who was called Maccabeus, Eleazar and Jonathan. When his time drew near to die, he charged them all: “Now hath pride and rebuke gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation: Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

The enemy was lifted up in pride, and it was a time of destruction for our people under the Greeks. The answer was not to bow but to be zealous for the law, and to be willing to give your life for the covenant of the fathers.

That charge is what the whole family fought on. Before he died, Mattathias set each son in his place, and the class is on the day of Simon, so Simon is not forgotten: the father who charged them to be zealous for the law went on to name Simon as the man of counsel and Judas as the captain, the brain and the hammer that would carry that zeal into battle.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Mattathias sets his sons in order: “behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel, give ear unto him alway: he shall be a father unto you.” Simon was a genius, a tactician. Always listen to Simon, because he is the brain of you; he will be the elder, so listen to him as a father and let him instruct you what to do.

“As for Judas Maccabeus, he hath been mighty and strong, even from his youth up: let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people.” Judas had hands from the beginning, so he would be the fighter. Judas was the warrior; he got the fame; he was the hammer. But every hammer needs a hand, and Simon was the mind behind the hammer: go here, go there, mobilize over here, have this many men with you. Simon the brain, Judas the brawn.

Our people fought the same way in Haiti. Toussaint Louverture's genius was to combine brilliant military strategy with statecraft. He turned a fractured rebellion into the most successful slave uprising in history, controlled all of Hispaniola by 1800, gave our people paid work and established order, and wrote a constitution that abolished slavery and made all equal, no light skin, no dark skin. Defying Napoleon cost him his life in a French prison, but his work made Haiti's independence possible in 1804.

The tactics Toussaint used against the French are the exact same tactics the family of the Maccabees used against the Greeks. Same tribe, same people, same playbook: Levi and Simeon together.

precepts.text: The bait-and-switch at Beth-horon: Judas hid his men in the heights and charged when the Greek column was congested in the narrow pass, the exact tactic Toussaint used to lure the French into a crossfire.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The same playbook is written out at Bethhoron. “Judas went forth to meet him with a small company: Who, when they saw the host coming to meet them, said unto Judas, How shall we be able, being so few, to fight against so great a multitude and so strong”. Judas answered, “with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: For the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven.” “They come against us in much pride and iniquity to destroy us, and our wives and children, and to spoil us: But we fight for our lives and our laws.”

That was the bait-and-switch ambush. The Greek army under Seron was marching down the narrow mountain pass of Bethhoron, and because the pass was tight they had to break their packed phalanx and march in a long, vulnerable column. Judas hid his men in the rocky heights, waited until the enemy was fully congested in the pass, then charged downhill. “he leapt suddenly upon them, and so Seron and his host was overthrown before him”, and they pursued them to the plain, “where were slain about eight hundred men of them; and the residue fled into the land of the Philistines.”

That is exactly what Toussaint did when he used a false retreat to lure the French into a crossfire. A small, under-equipped force facing a professional superpower empire could not win in an open field, so it used the terrain, strategic retreats and the ambush. Do not be surprised if Toussaint read Maccabees. It is the same people fighting the same way, and the strength comes from heaven.

precepts.text: Assembled with one accord, they sent chosen men, Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Bishops, deacons, and captains on one accord send chosen men who risk their lives in the hoods of Haiti, Africa, and Puerto Rico. Michael Jordan is not risking anything. And leaders build leaders: a father wants his son to be better than him, and a leader whose mindset is job security in the high seat will be removed.
precepts.point: Public service announcement: IUIC is not a fractured organization; with the Most High we are thriving. Passover season is coming and the tree gets shaken, so do not fall out of it over Easter with your mother's white dress and tall hat.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Mattathias would not do what everybody else was doing. He cried, “Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.” Somebody had to stand up, and that is the mark of a true leader. Acts shows what the leaders of the church were doing: “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Assembled with one accord: bishops on one accord, deacons on one accord, captains on one accord. And they send chosen men, not just anybody. You could say they send out Bishop Nathanyel and Deacon Isaac, as they sent Barnabas and Paul.

“Men that have hazarded their lives”: a real leader risks his life for Christ. They call Michael Jordan a leader, football coaches leaders of men; Michael Jordan is not risking anything. Wyclef, what are you doing? The men of this camp have been to Haiti, to Africa, to the barrios of Puerto Rico. They are not going to the suburbs; they are going to the hood, all over IUIC, putting their lives on the line for the name of Christ.

And leaders build leaders. That is an attribute of a father: a father wants his son to be better than him. The bishops are building leadership, sending men to countries and corners that could not be touched before, and now others have been raised up to touch them. But if your mindset is job security, sitting in the high seat, and not building brothers to be better than yourself, forget about it: the Lord will remove you.

precepts.text: If you hear it and do not utter it you bear the iniquity: that is why when you hear evil among us, you tell it.
precepts.point: Saying all of this raises the bounty on your head, because in Babylon the Great nobody is supposed to teach you the truth; a prophet among the slaves who taught the Bible would be hunted and killed, like Nat Turner.

precepts.text: That all speak the same thing and that there be no divisions among you. The decree only worked because every man there had the same mind.
precepts.point: Our forefathers had to make that decision and every man there had to have the same mind. That is the decision in front of us too: get to camp, get out to war, endure hardness, and drop the victim mindset.

precepts.text: Phinehas saw an Israelite bring his Midianitish woman before the whole weeping congregation, rose up, took a javelin and thrust them both through, and the plague was stayed. Mattathias was a Levite inspired by his own Levite kinsman.
precepts.point: He ran and slew him on the altar, killed the king's commissioner who compelled men to sacrifice, and pulled the altar down. Pulling that altar down was the Levite's office.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

precepts.text: Our God is able to deliver us and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king — but if not, we will not serve thy gods nor worship the golden image. Even unrescued they were willing to die for what they believed, and we have to get to that mindset.
precepts.point: When you go through things — health, children leaving this truth, the job, a wife or a husband who does not believe — go back to your forefathers, who went through things as well. It is harder for us: they all knew they were the Israelites, and our people have been cut off from that.

precepts.text: Be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.
precepts.point: Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
The wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain the covenant of peace. Mattathias said it to his sons: “Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

Be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. That covenant of peace, rest from this servitude of bondage, is what all of us are striving for, and zeal for the law is how it is obtained.

precepts.text: Phinehas obtained the everlasting priesthood by being zealous and fervent.
precepts.point: Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
The Lord gave Phinehas “the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God.” Mattathias set him before his sons as the pattern: “Phinees our father in being zealous and fervent obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.”

Phinehas our father obtained it by being zealous and fervent. That is the wisdom in reading his acts: be zealous for the law of the Most High, and the covenant of peace all of us are striving for is obtained the same way.

precepts.text: Abraham drew down with the knife even when it made no fleshly sense, and Joseph, betrayed and tempted, kept the commandment in the time of his distress and was exalted to be lord of Egypt; loyalty to the Lord regardless of circumstances is what the trial is for.
precepts.point: The Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart to be captain over his people. Samuel prophesied this without ever having met the replacement; that man is David, predestined before he is even introduced in the scriptures.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel does not entertain the excuses: “Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee”. Saul thought he was only bending Samuel’s word, but disobeying the instruction was disobeying the commandment of the Lord. For that one act of foolishness the Lord withdrew what he would have given, Saul’s lineage ruling Israel: “for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever. But now thy kingdom shall not continue”.

The Lord wants to see whether you will perform what he told you to do even when things do not work out how you planned. “Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness?” Abraham drew down with the knife even when it made no fleshly sense. “Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment and was made lord of Egypt.” Joseph was betrayed and tempted, kept the commandment, and was exalted.

Loyalty to the Lord regardless of circumstances is what the trial is for. That is what proves you faithful in temptation and worthy of being exalted, and Saul failed that test in the time of his distress.

precepts.text: What nation hath not had a part in her kingdom, and gotten of her spoils? All her ornaments are taken away; of a free woman she is become a bondslave.
precepts.point: He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.

note.label: Zechariah 9: Thy King Cometh Unto Thee, Just and Having Salvation

precepts.why:
Tyrus, Zidon, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the Philistines are judged for the part they had in the captivity, and they had a part. “What nation hath not had a part in her kingdom and gotten of her spoils? All her ornaments are taken away; of a free woman she is become a bondslave.”

Every nation had a part in Israel's kingdom and got of her spoils; of a free woman she became a bondslave. That is why Tyrus is cast out and devoured with fire, and the pride of the Philistines cut off.

precepts.text: Our religion was always the law and the ordinances of the fathers, never the man-made traditions taught in slavery.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
What was the Jews' religion Paul profited in? “God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.” Our religion was always the law and the ordinances of the fathers, never the man-made traditions taught in slavery.

So when Paul speaks of profiting in the Jews' religion, that is the law and the ordinances. Saul kept it zealously before Christ appeared to him in the way, and Christ, not the apostles, taught him from there.

precepts.text: Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, from whom came the Hasmonean dynasty, meaning the house of Simeon.
precepts.point: Mattathias and the Hasmonean dynasty, the house of Simeon, along with the Assideans who were later called Pharisees, went about circumcising valiantly and restoring the law.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and dwelt in Modin.”

Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon: from him came the Hasmonean dynasty, meaning the house of Simeon. He and his house are the ones who went about restoring the law and circumcision.

precepts.text: The Assideans, mighty men devoted to the law, joined Mattathias and circumcised the uncircumcised valiantly. The Jewish Encyclopedia notes the Assideans, or Hasidim, were pious men devoted to the law from whom the Pharisees are held to have developed.
precepts.point: Mattathias and the Hasmonean dynasty, the house of Simeon, along with the Assideans who were later called Pharisees, went about circumcising valiantly and restoring the law.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Then came there unto him a company of Assideans who were mighty men of Israel, even all such as were voluntarily devoted unto the law.”

“Then Mattathias and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars: And what children soever they found within the coast of Israel uncircumcised, those they circumcised valiantly.” The Assideans, mighty men devoted to the law, joined Mattathias and circumcised the uncircumcised valiantly. The Jewish Encyclopedia notes that the Assideans, or Hasidim, were pious men devoted to the law, from whom the Pharisees are held to have developed.

So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees, who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments. The uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites. That is who contended with Peter.

precepts.point: He called himself the chief of sinners. 2 Corinthians 12:7 says a thorn in the flesh was given to him, the messenger of Satan, lest he be exalted above measure.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul's “conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion” refers to the laws of his fathers. Religion comes from the Latin word religio, meaning to bind, to restrain, to withhold you from your lust. First Maccabees defines religion as the law and the ordinances: “Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.”

To go from the religion is to forsake the law and the ordinances. So the Jews' religion Paul was zealous in was the law and the traditions of his fathers, and he was “more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers” than his equals.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left. To do what? Go from our religion. When you leave the law, statutes and commandments, you are leaving the religion that was given unto you. You cannot unite under any other banner, under any other religion. Our religion is the faith of Christ and the commandments. Understand that.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Mattathias refused, and because of that he and his sons faced persecution and became fugitives on the run. And many joined them, choosing to be honorable the way he was. But many of my brothers today want honor and greatness in Babylon, Babylonian greatness, not God's. You cannot be a captive and get king privileges. Either you are in captivity or you are free. King is a term of endearment, but in reality, whether you make four figures or seven figures, you are a captive here.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: The king's officers came to Mattathias: thou art a ruler, and an honourable and great man in this city; come thou first and fulfil the king's commandment, like as all the heathen have done, yea, and the men of Judah also; so shalt thou and thy house be in the number of the king's friends, and thou and thy children shall be honoured with silver and gold, and many rewards. That is what sold to do mischief means: money. I am going to teach Christianity because I want money. I am going to teach against God's laws because I want money. Fame, fortune, the finer things in life.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: Mattathias had five sons, and the class is on the day of Simon, so Simon is not forgotten: Judas was the hammer and Simon was the hand behind it.

points: Mattathias answered with a loud voice: though all the nations under the king's dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers.

points: God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand or the left. Our religion is keeping the commandments.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Let us die all in our innocency: heaven and earth shall testify for us, that ye put us to death wrongfully. Our fathers said it under the Greeks, and the record repeats under every power since: heaven and earth testify for the innocent blood.

note.label: They Say We Hate White People

points: What nation hath not had a part in her kingdom, and gotten of her spoils? Almost every kingdom had a hand in our demise and enslavement. That is why they cannot stop talking about it; the Lord constantly reminds them, and he is using his servants in the highways to teach the atrocities that happened to us and pull our people out of the fire. The Lord does not want to destroy his people; he wants their deliverance. But some of them are so hard headed they have to go.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: You have to see it before you see it. Before anything happens you visualize it, whether graduating, marrying, or getting a job. Mattathias saw two realities, one where his children ate swine like everybody else and one where they fought and won, and refused the first.
Though all nations obey the king, yet will I and my sons walk in the covenant of our fathers. Religion is keeping the commandments; God forbid we forsake the law.

Christ is King of kings, the boss of all bosses, so conduct yourself as a boss and do not take your hand off the plow like Jonah.

points: When a Jew sacrificed at Modin he was inflamed with zeal, slew him on the altar, killed the king's commissioner, pulled down the altar, and cried, whosoever is zealous of the law, let him follow me. Somebody had to stand up.

points: Mattathias stood against what every nation under the king's dominion was doing, and it took anger to have that kind of resolve.

points: God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances: not bending at all, neither to the right hand nor to the left.

points: One of the Jews came in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar at Modin, according to the king's commandment; people are supposed to be afraid to come before you with that, and he was not afraid at all.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Mattathias was inflamed with zeal, and zeal there is anger: his reins trembled and he could not forbear to shew his anger, and that anger is what gave him the strength to run and slay him upon the altar.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: He killed the king's commissioner too, the one compelling men to sacrifice, and pulled the altar down.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God, so his anger was the result of keeping God's commandments.
Like as Phinees did unto Zambri: Phinees saw the sin going on with the women of Moab, and the Lord was pleased and did not destroy Israel because of that righteous anger.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Whosoever is zealous of the law and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me, and the rest go to hell: the same choice Moses put to Israel.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: He and his sons fled into the mountains and left everything they had in the city.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Whole families got up and moved, children, wives and cattle, because afflictions increased sore upon them.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: It was told the king's servants that men who had broken the king's commandment were gone down into the secret places in the wilderness, so our own people told on us and were in a pact with the Greeks.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: They made war against them on the sabbath day, which means they had studied us and knew we would not fight on that day.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Come forth and do according to the commandment of the king and ye shall live: follow Satan and we will let you live, and you pay for it in the end.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: We will not come forth, neither will we do the king's commandment to profane the sabbath day, so they gave them the battle with all speed.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: They answered them not, neither cast they a stone, and did not even stop the places where they lay hid.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Let us die all in our innocency: they would have fought, but not on that day. This was keeping the sabbath commandment, not fear.
Heaven and earth will testify for us that ye put us to death wrongfully is a prayer for vengeance: God will judge you for what you did to his people. Christians do not think that way.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: They rose up against them on the sabbath and slew them with their wives and children and their cattle, to the number of a thousand people.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: Mattathias and his friends mourned for them right sore, because they were murdered.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: If we fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth: at some point the anger has to kick in, because these people have no conscience.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: So they decreed that whosoever comes to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: The Assideans, mighty men of Israel voluntarily devoted unto the law, came to him, and all that fled for persecution joined themselves unto them and were a stay unto them.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: They joined their forces and smote sinful men in their anger and wicked men in their wrath, and the rest fled to the heathen for succour because Mattathias and his sons were on the hunt.
That is what has to happen among us now, spiritually: wicked sinful people have to go, and it takes anger to make sure there is no love for sin going on in here.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

points: They pulled down the altars and took the filth out, and the children they found uncircumcised they circumcised: you keep the laws or you do not live.

points: Wherefore was I born to see the misery of my people: the city into the hand of the enemy, the sanctuary into the hand of strangers.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: He saw the blasphemies committed in Judah and Jerusalem and said woe is me, wherefore was I born to see the misery of my people. That is a Levite watching the sanctuary delivered into the hand of strangers.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: "Her temple is become as a man without glory." The temple was his office, and that is why the rage was in him.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: "Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me." For the ones who did not follow him, the decree stood and the books were burned — they lost the tradition of their fathers and were looked at as sellouts.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: He and his sons fled into the mountains and left everything they ever had in the city. All five were trained up by him and all five went. There was no conversation about not going; they were perfectly joined together in the same mind.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Then many that sought after justice and judgment went down into the wilderness with their wives, their children and their cattle.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: When the word got back, whose name do you think came up? They pursued after them with a great number, overtook them and made war on them on the Sabbath day.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: One group had decided they would not raise a sword on the Sabbath — if they are taken out, everyone will know the stories that they were innocent. They were slaughtered, and Mattathias and his friends mourned for them right sore.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: One said to another: if we all do as our brethren have done and fight not for our lives and laws, they will quickly root us out of the earth.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: So they decreed it — whosoever comes to make battle with us on the Sabbath day, we will fight against him. We are going to live together or die together, and if we die we die fighting.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: A company of Assideans came to him — a company is organised men, like a battalion or a platoon — and they were mighty men of Israel, voluntarily devoted unto the law.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Then all those who fled for persecution joined themselves to them and were a stay unto them. Men who would not stay among the sellouts and had nowhere to go heard about it and came.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: They joined their forces and smote sinful men in their anger. They knocked the altars down, circumcised the children valiantly and recovered the books of the law.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers — then call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time, and so receive great honour and an everlasting name.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment and was made lord of Egypt. Thrown in the hole, sold, bound in prison, and he fled the act of adultery from Potiphar's wife like fleeing from the face of a serpent.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Then Phinees our father, zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: He had just finished the speech about being zealous of the law and not being oppressed, and here comes a dumb, stupid Israelite to sacrifice on the altar at Modin in the sight of everybody.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Mattathias was inflamed with zeal and his reins trembled — the brother was shaking — and he could not forbear to show his anger according to judgment.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: He ran and slew him on the altar, killed the king's commissioner who compelled men to sacrifice, and pulled the altar down. Pulling that altar down was the Levite's office.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: On his deathbed he was still making sure his sons understood what they had to do, and he reached for the three holy children who by believing were saved out of the flame.
He knew that history because his father and his grandfather taught him the laws and the history, and as a man he knew he might have to go through the same thing one day.

When you go through things — health, children leaving this truth, the job, a wife or a husband who does not believe — go back to your forefathers, who went through things as well. It is harder for us: they all knew they were the Israelites, and our people have been cut off from that.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. That is what the Feast of Dedication is: the warriors' feast.

Shout out to all the brothers that have been putting in the work -- 30 days of camp, 60 days, 100 days, 365 days. It does not matter how many days you are doing, as long as you are out there fighting for the laws and fighting for the nation.

If you are not ready to give your life for this truth, get the hell out of the way. We are looking for the brothers that are ready to give their lives for the laws of God. We are looking for the ultimate warriors.
We fight for our men, we fight for the women, we fight for the children, we fight for our people, and when our people call upon us we show up. They are not calling on these Christian pastors.
They have no answers and no solutions. We have the solution.

note.label: CHRIST: ISRAEL'S LAST TEMPLE

points: But they said, we will not come forth, neither will we do the king's commandment to profane the sabbath day. We are not conforming.
Do not betray the laws of God and do not betray your God.
We are not betraying the Lord because we want something in this nation, and we are not going to keep lying down in shame.
Keep applying the pressure on this earth. Do not stop, do not give up, become more temperate, more patient, more godly.
